walkthrough:
A repeated root supplies the contact coordinate once the gradient is known.
Substitute $y = mx$ into $(x - 4)^2 + y^2 = 4$:
$$x^2 - 8x + 16 + m^2x^2 = 4$$
$$(1 + m^2)x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $\Delta = 0$:
$$\Delta = (-8)^2 - 4(1 + m^2)(12) = 0$$
$$64 - 48 - 48m^2 = 0$$
$$16 - 48m^2 = 0 \implies 3m^2 - 1 = 0 \implies m = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

hints: The $x$-coordinate of the contact point is the repeated root: $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = \dfrac{8}{2(1 + 1/3)} = \dfrac{8}{8/3} = 3$.
walkthrough:
A repeated root supplies the contact coordinate once the gradient is known.
For a tangent, the quadratic $(1 + m^2)x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0$ has a repeated root $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$:
$$x = \dfrac{8}{2(1 + m^2)} = \dfrac{8}{2(1 + 1/3)} = \dfrac{8}{8/3} = 3$$

Substitute $x = 3$ into the tangent equations $y = mx$:
$$\text{For } m = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}: \quad y = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3} \implies P(3, \sqrt{3})$$
$$\text{For } m = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}: \quad y = -\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = -\sqrt{3} \implies Q(3, -\sqrt{3})$$
